chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about buying palm trees, vineyards, and fruits for three or four years. He said, 'There is no harm in it. He means: if it does not produce in this year, it will produce in the next. And if you buy it for one year, do not buy it until it matures. And if you buy it for three years before it matures, there is no harm.'

And he was asked about a man who buys named fruit from a land, and that entire land perishes. He said, 'They disputed that matter before the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). They would keep mentioning it, and when he saw that they did not cease the dispute, he forbade them from that sale until the fruit matures, but he did not forbid it completely; he did so because of their dispute.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy fruit trees for multiple years before they bear fruit?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) permits purchasing fruit-bearing trees for multiple years prior to maturity, emphasizing that if the fruit does not yield in one year, it may be harvested in the next, provided the transaction is clear. In a distinct case concerning named fruit where land destruction caused persistent litigation (khushum), the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited the sale temporarily not as an intrinsic invalidity (haram), but as a pragmatic measure to resolve disputes, illustrating the Shia principle of 'sulh' (conciliation) in commercial jurisprudence.
